---
title: "Two targets of one kind"
filters:
  - index
---

A term with two or more cross-reference targets of one kind prints that kind's
word once, in front of all of them. This document and its twin,
`xref-joined-separator.qmd`, carry the same body and differ only in whether the
metadata declares the punctuation between two cross-references.

Every subject term below is marked only where its own section says, and each
section is a page of its own, so the one page number this fixture prints for a
subject term is the page its plain mark is on. Inside each kind of
cross-reference the targets are written in the reverse of alphabetical order,
so an index that sorted them would print them in another order than the one
written here.

## Two see targets

A term that points two places: [Quince]{.index see="Zinnia"} and
[Quince]{.index see="Aster"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Two see-also targets

A term with two further places to look: [Rowan]{.index see-also="Yarrow"} and
[Rowan]{.index see-also="Bramble"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Four targets of two kinds

A term whose first mark is a see-also, and whose two kinds alternate:
[Sorrel]{.index see-also="Moss"}, [Sorrel]{.index see="Zed"},
[Sorrel]{.index see-also="Fern"} and [Sorrel]{.index see="Ash"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## A plain mark and two see targets

A term marked plainly, [Tansy]{.index}, and pointing two places:
[Tansy]{.index see="Wort"} and [Tansy]{.index see="Clover"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## The targets

Every target above is a term of its own, marked here so each cross-reference
names an entry the index prints: [Zinnia]{.index}, [Aster]{.index},
[Yarrow]{.index}, [Bramble]{.index}, [Moss]{.index}, [Zed]{.index},
[Fern]{.index}, [Ash]{.index}, [Wort]{.index} and [Clover]{.index}.
